question.text: SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations covers:

answer.text: Comprehensive guidelines on trading, clearing, settlement, risk management, membership, and investor services
Only the listing requirements for companies
Only the fee structure of exchanges
Guidelines applicable only to newly established exchanges

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI issues a Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations that consolidates the regulatory directions applicable to these market infrastructure institutions. In practice, it covers comprehensive guidelines on trading, clearing, settlement, risk management, membership criteria, surveillance and investor services — bringing together previously issued circulars into a single, navigable document. The Trap: The Master Circular is not limited to listing requirements, is not just a fee schedule, and does not apply only to newly established exchanges. It is broad in scope and applies to all SEBI-recognised exchanges and clearing corporations. Note: The full scope of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations is not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages only reference a specific Master Circular clause on contract size and a Chapter 8 learning-objective summary. The framing above reflects general SEBI Master Circular knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
